headline: Red Sox bullpen stumbles again in heartbreaker loss to Athletics
morning_brew: Watching that ninth inning last night was like staring into the abyss, and frankly, I'm just sick of it. A 4-3 loss to the Athletics at Fenway isn't just another mark in the L column, it's a gut punch that leaves you questioning everything we thought we knew about this pitching staff. We had the lead, we had the momentum, and then the whole thing just unraveled in a way that made me want to throw my cold Dunks right at the screen. I been sayin' it all year, you cannot expect to make a serious run if you're just gifting games away in the final frame.

The arson squad really outdid themselves this time, blowing a lead and letting the Athletics walk away with a win that should've stayed in the Hub. My mother watched the last three innings and didn't even say a word, she just went to bed, and honestly that's the only sane response to a collapse like that. We had our chances to put them away earlier, but the bats went cold when it mattered most, leaving us looking at a sour result that ruins what should've been a perfect summer night at the oldest yard in baseball.

We're off to Toronto now, and we better find our footing quick before this little slump turns into a full-blown crisis. I’m not saying the season is over, but we’re drifting away from that high-octane energy we saw just a few days ago, and the boys need to wake up. It’s a long flight to Canada, and I hope they spend the whole time thinking about how to close out a game without making the rest of us age ten years in nine innings.

news_digest.headline: Athletics' Wilson sets record with 111 errorless games in row
news_digest.dans_take: I respect the glove, I really do, but watching him set a record at Fenway while we handed him the win is just plain torture.

news_digest.headline: Don Nelson, second-winningest coach in NBA history, dies at 86
news_digest.dans_take: A true legend of the game who changed how it was played, he'll be missed by anyone who loves basketball.
